title: Warmth gave no clear change in hearing-impairment links to frog records in four US samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether survey-night warmth changed the link between reported hearing impairment and the number of four frog species heard at a stop. We used 102,807 NAAMP stop visits on 725 routes in two eastern US regions and two periods in 2001-2015. Models compared stops on the same survey run and controlled fixed site-by-window differences, local temperature, and month and state differences in the noise slope. All four 98.75 percent route-cluster intervals for the change per 5 C included zero. Added observer control, removal of listening breaks, and two-way route and year intervals did not give a repeated clear change. Hearing impairment had a negative average association in each sample. Subjective noise reports, selected survey nights, missing temperature data and unmeasured calling activity limit the result. This is a test of recorded calling, not true richness, climate trends or air-pollutant effects.
